newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar closes on lows on political concern.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar closes on lows on political concern.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed on its lows for the day at US$0.6920/25, pushed down by comments from Labour leader Helen Clark, after trading as high as 0.6935. A dealer said while no further samurai issues had been confirmed, there were signs of related activity.

"Further Euro-kiwi interest done this week had a compounding effect. People putting on bearish structures helped push the kiwi lower. At close to its 0.6950 recent highs, people are looking at the election," the dealer said.

New Zealand faces a general election on October 12. Labour leader Clark told Reuters in an interview she was prepared to include the left-wing Alliance in policy negotiations if it committed to supporting her party on confidence votes after the election.
"Helen Clark welcoming Anderton's post-election stance also had a depressing effect on sentiment," the dealer said.
On the Trade Weighted Index, the kiwi closed at 65.63 against an opening of 65.66.
"With the current levels, it is a good time to put bearish structures on and that brought some of the supply into the market today," the dealer said.
He said the kiwi should hold at 0.6910 to 0.6915 overnight. "With yields moving up late in the day there will be more talk of samurais tomorrow which will keep it fairly perky."
Another dealer said the kiwi would not trade out of a 0.6915-35 range overnight. "The major excitement for the day was Clark's comments on a possible deal with the Alliance," he said.
